title: The 5-Star Confidence System
intro: Put a star rating next to every finding so stakeholders see at a glance how much to trust it. Stars rise as evidence accumulates.

learn.title: The scale
learn.text:
★☆☆☆☆ — one attitudinal finding, or a secondary source
★★☆☆☆ — at least one behavioural finding, best practice or technical fact; or two or more attitudinal
★★★☆☆ — three or more findings, including at least one behavioural, best-practice or factual
★★★★☆ — as above, and replicated
★★★★★ — well established; validated repeatedly across studies

Calabro has used this for more than seven years. Stakeholders learn it in seconds.

try.q: A finding rests on one survey question. How many stars?
options: None — it shouldn't be in the repository
try.explain: A single attitudinal finding is the bottom of the scale.

learn.title: Why it works
learn.text:
Nobody needs a statistics lecture: **three stars says “solid, may need more validation”**.

It becomes shorthand in difficult conversations, it encourages teams to check the repository before commissioning a new study, and it makes clear when a recommendation rests on one survey answer.

try.q: What does the system change in a difficult conversation?
options: It gives everyone shared shorthand for confidence
It settles which finding is correct
It removes the need for a readout
It assigns ownership of the decision
try.explain: Three stars means “solid, may need more validation” without a statistics lecture.

left.label: Without stars
items: Every finding reads as equally certain

learn.title: The Bayesian habit underneath
learn.text:
**Start from priors** — best practices from NN/g and MeasuringU are prior knowledge, not a blank slate.

**Update with each study** rather than treating every project as the first look at the question.

**Communicate uncertainty** as a level, not a yes/no.

The stars are the practical, visible form of that habit.

options: What you already know before the study
try.explain: Established best practice counts as prior knowledge.

test.q: What is the star rating attached to?
test.explain: So confidence travels with the finding.

test.q: What does four stars require that three doesn't?
What behaviour does the system encourage before a new study?
test.explain: Existing evidence may already be at three or four stars.

test.q: Why is a Michelin-style scale useful for stakeholders?
options: It can be automated from the data

test.q: How long has Calabro used this system?
test.explain: Long enough to see it become team shorthand.
